To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the securitizing actors in North Korea and Madagascar have successfully securitized food/nutrition, but the success is limited by the lack of the securitizers’ legitimacy and the securitized actors’ resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how food insecurity is constructed as a threat to national security in North Korea and Madagascar, and what the implications of such a securitization are.
the question of whether food/nutrition insecurity should be considered as a threat to the state and its people.
the question of how and why food insecurity has become a matter of security.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the securitisation of food/nutritional insecurity is a process of construction, which is not only dependent on the nature of the threat itself, but also the context in which it takes place.
the securitizing actor, the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) in this case, is not only the one who is securitizing the food/nutrient issue but also the securitizers of the securitizations.
food security is a matter of security.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are looking into the securitisation of food and how this has been done in the past, but also how it is being done in the present.
we are not just looking for the right food, but also the right way to feed it.

food security is not a traditional security issue, but it can be securitized in the case of North Korea and in Madagascar, where food insecurity is a serious problem and a threat to the survival of the state.

the securitisation of food is not only about food, but also about power.
